project.name: Titan AI
project.description: Autonomous software engineering operating system, implemented as Titan Core: seven cooperating engines (Planner, Orchestrator, Context, Knowledge, Execution, Validation, Learning). See architecture.md Section 7 and decisions.md ADR-0002.

next_phase.name: Maintenance & Continuous Improvement
next_phase.blocked_reason: Awaiting Phase 016 completion. Phase 016's Milestones 1-6 are implemented and verified (CI restoration, production promotion mechanism, deploy mechanics, post-deploy verification, monitoring/alerting policy, a genuine rollback exercise), but no production deployment has occurred. No agent working this repository has authenticated GitHub write/dispatch access; a human with repository access must trigger the deploy-production job via the GitHub Actions UI before Phase 016's Exit Criteria can be honestly checked.

tech_stack.notes: Selected TypeScript with Node.js, npm workspaces, Vitest, ESLint, and Prettier for the initial Titan AI monorepo scaffold (see tech_stack.md and ADR-0003).

architecture.notes: architecture.md Section 7 defines the approved Titan Core engine architecture (7 engines), with security architecture governance established in Section 6.

engines.name: Planner Engine
engines.notes: createPlan, validatePlan, optimizePlan, estimatePlan, and explainPlan are implemented (Milestones 1-6). cancelPlan remains a NotImplementedError stub; not required by any Phase 008 exit criterion.

engines.name: Orchestrator Engine
engines.notes: orchestrate, executeWorkflow, getWorkflowStatus, pauseWorkflow, resumeWorkflow, cancelWorkflow, and dispatchWorkflow are all implemented (Milestones 1-7). All seven public API methods are implemented with no remaining NotImplementedError stubs. Dispatch and escalation are structural only; no scheduling, execution, retries, or cross-engine runtime calls.

engines.name: Context Engine
engines.notes: Phase 013 Milestone 1 added ContextEngine, extending BaseEngine and implementing the shared lifecycle contract (initialize/start/stop/health/metadata/version/contractVersion/getState) via specification/engine_api.md §3.1; composes the pre-existing ContextManager unchanged; declares capabilities: [] since no repository document names a Context Engine business method.

engines.name: Execution Engine
engines.notes: execute, getExecutionStatus, and reportResult are implemented (Milestones 1-5: runtime foundation, complete planned domain model, ExecutionBuilder/execute() - deterministic structural translation of an Orchestrator WorkflowDispatchResult into an ExecutionRecord, ExecutionValidator/getExecutionStatus() - deterministic structural validation of an ExecutionRecord, and ExecutionStatusTracker/reportResult() - deterministic structural summarization of an ExecutionRecord; despite its name, reportResult() performs no real result reporting). cancelExecution remains an unimplemented NotImplementedError stub; a dedicated governance review (see phases/phase-010-execution-engine-implementation.md) confirmed this is not required by any Phase 010 exit criterion, since the 'dispatch-to-result lifecycle' phrase used in the exit criteria is never defined anywhere in the repository.

engines.name: Validation Engine
engines.notes: validate and getValidationStatus are implemented (Milestones 1-5: runtime foundation, complete planned domain model, ValidationBuilder/validate() - deterministic structural translation of an Execution Engine ExecutionSummary/ExecutionRecord into a ValidationPipelineResult, ValidationValidator/getValidationStatus() - deterministic structural validation of a ValidationVerdict, and ValidationEvidenceCollector/ValidationPipelineRunner - deterministic structural evidence collection composed with verdict construction, wired into validate()). approveValidation and rejectValidation remain unimplemented NotImplementedError stubs; a dedicated specification audit and governance review (see phases/phase-011-validation-engine-implementation.md) confirmed neither is required by any Phase 011 exit criterion or specification/engine_api.md requirement, and that implementing them would require either persistence (a validation store/lookup mechanism) or business logic (approval authority/audit semantics), both out of scope for deterministic structural processing.

engines.name: Learning Engine
engines.notes: observeCycle, generateProposal, prepareKnowledgeHandoff, and analyzeCycle are implemented (Milestones 1-6: runtime foundation, complete domain model, LearningObservationBuilder/observeCycle(), LearningProposalBuilder/generateProposal(), LearningKnowledgeHandoffBuilder/prepareKnowledgeHandoff(), and LearningLessonBuilder/LearningFlaggedRiskBuilder/LearningProposedAdrBuilder/LearningPipelineBuilder/analyzeCycle()). All four public API methods are implemented with no remaining NotImplementedError stubs. A dedicated Governance Resolution (see phases/phase-012-learning-engine-implementation.md) determined that actual Knowledge Engine-side consumption of Learning Engine handoff artifacts is architecturally assigned to the Knowledge Engine and to Phase 013's cross-engine validation scope, not to Phase 012; it remains unimplemented and unscoped pending Phase 013 or a future ADR.

titan_core.notes: Implementation order follows the Titan Core architecture data-flow dependency order: Context first, then the shared framework, then security governance, then Knowledge, Planner, Orchestrator, Execution, Validation, and Learning. Phase 013 (Titan Core Integration and Hardening) is complete: all seven engines are wired into apps/titan-shell via the shared EngineRegistry, end-to-end and cross-engine-boundary integration tests exist (tests/integration/), and a security/performance hardening review is recorded at .titan/reviews/2026-07-31-phase-013-security-performance-hardening.md. Phase 014 (Test Coverage Completion) is complete: coverage reporting infrastructure (npm run coverage), Knowledge Engine/LifecycleManager/ContextManager coverage gap closures, and a CI quality-gate workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) were added, with three unresolved items carried forward (npm audit findings not yet remediated/risk-accepted, unenforced coverage thresholds pending a domain/application folder-mapping decision, and a confirmed reproducible flaky test in tests/unit/validation-engine.test.ts). No engine's business logic changed during Phase 013 or Phase 014. Phase 015 (Deployment Readiness) is complete (2026-08-07), across ten milestones: three CI-gate additions to .github/workflows/ci.yml (format-check, no-skipped-tests, basic secrets pattern scan); the deployment-target governance decision (ADR-0008: local/CLI execution, no external hosting provider, tech_stack.md §5); dependency vulnerability remediation (npm audit 8 → 0); artifact packaging with clean-environment validation (scripts/package-artifact.sh, the validate-artifact CI job); the Staging Environment (a GitHub `staging` environment, deployment restricted to `main`, configured via repository Settings); Staging Validation (612/612 tests passed against the packaged artifact in a clean, freshly-provisioned environment — a local reproduction, not yet evidenced by a live GitHub Actions run); documentation gap closure (security_checklist.md's Pre-Deployment Checklist cross-referenced and classified; a code/security/incident-response-plan review produced, .titan/reviews/2026-08-07-phase-015-documentation-and-incident-readiness-review.md); and a Phase 015/016 boundary correction determining that Production Deployment and Rollback execution belong to Phase 016 (phase-016-production-release.md's own Objective/Scope), not Phase 015, whose Exit Criterion 3 ("Production release can proceed under governance controls") is a readiness/capability statement rather than a claim that a deployment occurred. All three Exit Criteria are satisfied and checked, including Exit Criterion 1's approval component, given by explicit human decision. Phase 016 (Production Release) began 2026-08-07: Milestone 1 restored the GitHub Actions pipeline (a hard format-check gate on 75 pre-existing .titan/ files had silently blocked every downstream step, including staging, on every run in this repository's history; fixed via .prettierignore plus an unrelated newly-disclosed js-yaml advisory fix; confirmed live-green on GitHub for the first time). Milestones 2-4 added a workflow_dispatch-only deploy-production job to ci.yml (never automatic by construction), reusing the exact staging-validated artifact via upload-artifact/download-artifact rather than rebuilding it, combining production deploy and post-deploy verification into one act since ADR-0008 means there is no live service to separately health-check. Milestone 5 extended deployment_strategy.md §6 (Monitoring & Alerting) with a policy grounded in what exists (CI pass/fail as the health signal, single-owner on-call, GitHub's default log retention). Milestone 6 genuinely exercised the rollback procedure against a prior known-good commit (build clean, 612/612 tests), logged in sessions/. No production deployment has occurred yet: no agent working this repository has authenticated GitHub write/dispatch access, so the actual trigger requires a human with repository access via the GitHub Actions UI. Phase 016's Exit Criteria remain unchecked pending that live event.

quality.notes: test_coverage_percent is the overall statement/line coverage reported by npm run coverage (Vitest v8 provider) as of Phase 014 closure; no per-tier (domain/application) threshold is enforced (see phases/phase-014-test-coverage-completion.md Review/Findings). known_open_test_issues counts the confirmed, reproducible flaky test in tests/unit/validation-engine.test.ts ('never reads policyRules or governanceRules'), tracked as a Phase 014 follow-up, not resolved. known_open_security_issues was 8 (3 moderate + 3 high + 2 critical) as reported in Phase 013's hardening review (devDependency transitives introduced when @vitest/coverage-v8 was installed); Phase 015 Milestone 5 remediated all 8 via a non-breaking npm audit fix plus a Vitest/@vitest/coverage-v8 upgrade to ^4.1.10 — npm audit now reports 0, so deployment_strategy.md §7's hard blocker on production deployment no longer applies.
